name: Rhodes
tagline: A Dodecanese island built around one of Europe's best-preserved medieval towns, its knights'-era walled Old Town paired with the clifftop Acropolis of Lindos and some of the Aegean's most reliable beaches.
highlight: The medieval Old Town of Rhodes, a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of Europe's largest inhabited medieval towns, its walls and knights'-era streets still standing largely intact.
shortDescription: A Dodecanese island pairing one of Europe's best-preserved medieval walled towns with the clifftop Acropolis of Lindos and dependable Aegean beaches.
metaDescription: A Rhodes travel guide: the medieval Old Town, Lindos and its Acropolis, the best beaches, when to go and a practical four-day itinerary.
knownFor: The medieval Old Town, Lindos, its beaches

image.file: File:City walls in Rhodes Old Town, Greece (51699456245).jpg
image.alt: The medieval walls and towers of Rhodes Old Town

intro: Rhodes' Old Town is one of Europe's largest and best-preserved inhabited medieval towns, built by the Knights Hospitaller after they took the island in 1309 and fortified it into one of the Crusader era's most formidable strongholds — its walls, gates and knights'-era streets still standing largely intact over seven centuries later.

That medieval core sits within a much older history — Rhodes was a significant power in the ancient Greek world, home to the Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and later passed through Byzantine, Ottoman and Italian rule before joining modern Greece, each leaving its own visible layer on the island.

Beyond the Old Town, Rhodes pairs the clifftop village and Acropolis of Lindos with genuinely dependable beaches and a mountainous, olive-and-vine-covered interior, giving the island real range beyond its famous medieval centre.

whyVisit.intro: Rhodes' case is that no other Dodecanese island pairs this significant a medieval town with this much genuine ancient history and reliable beach time.

points.title: The Old Town is genuinely one of Europe's great medieval towns
points.text: A UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the continent's largest inhabited medieval towns, its knights'-era fortifications still substantially intact.

points.title: Lindos pairs genuine ancient and medieval history
points.text: An acropolis with ancient Greek temple ruins layered beneath a medieval castle, above a genuinely striking whitewashed village.

points.title: The beaches are genuinely reliable
points.text: A long, sunny season and a real range of coastline, from organised resort beaches to quieter coves further from the main towns.

points.title: The island's history runs genuinely deep
points.text: Ancient Greek, Byzantine, Crusader, Ottoman and Italian layers are all visibly present across the island.

points.title: It connects well to the wider Dodecanese and beyond
points.text: Ferries reach Symi, Kos and other Dodecanese islands, with seasonal connections to Crete, genuinely widening a Rhodes-based trip.

attractionsIntro: Rhodes' essential sights, from its medieval walled town to its clifftop acropolis and ancient ruins.

attractions.name: The Old Town of Rhodes

image.alt: The fortified medieval walls of Rhodes Old Town

attractions.text: One of Europe's largest and best-preserved inhabited medieval towns, its knights'-era walls, gates and cobbled streets forming a genuine UNESCO World Heritage site.
attractions.tip: Walk the full circuit of the outer walls, partially open to visitors — a genuinely different perspective on the town's scale than exploring the streets alone.

attractions.name: The Palace of the Grand Master

image.alt: The fortified Palace of the Grand Master in Rhodes

attractions.text: The Knights Hospitaller's imposing fortified palace, genuinely one of the Old Town's most significant buildings, restored with mosaic floors and period furnishings.
attractions.tip: The palace's upper floor rooms are genuinely worth the extra time — many visitors only see the ground-floor halls.

attractions.name: The Street of the Knights

image.alt: The medieval Street of the Knights in Rhodes Old Town

attractions.text: A genuinely atmospheric medieval street lined with the former inns of the Knights Hospitaller's various language groups, among Europe's best-preserved medieval streetscapes.
attractions.tip: Visit early morning for the street largely to yourself, before Old Town crowds build through the day.

attractions.name: Lindos and its Acropolis

image.file: File:Lindos. View of the Acropolis and town from the north-east. Rhodes, Greece.jpg
image.alt: Lindos village beneath its clifftop Acropolis

attractions.text: A dramatic clifftop acropolis layering ancient Greek temple ruins beneath a medieval castle, above a genuinely striking whitewashed village and bay.
attractions.tip: Take the donkey ride or walk up early to beat both the heat and the day-trip crowds from Rhodes Town.

attractions.name: The Valley of the Butterflies

image.alt: The shaded forest valley of the Valley of the Butterflies

attractions.text: A genuinely shaded, cool forest valley that hosts a large seasonal gathering of Jersey tiger moths each summer, a distinctive natural attraction.
attractions.tip: Visit between June and September for the moths — outside that window, the valley is a pleasant walk without the main draw.

attractions.name: Ancient Kamiros

image.alt: The ruins of the ancient city of Kamiros

attractions.text: The well-preserved ruins of one of Rhodes' three ancient city-states, genuinely less visited than Lindos despite its comparable archaeological significance.
attractions.tip: The site offers genuinely little shade — bring water and a hat, particularly in summer.

thingsToDoIntro: Beyond the Old Town and Lindos, Rhodes rewards its beaches, its wider Dodecanese connections and its genuinely serious food culture.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the medieval Old Town's walls and moat

image.file: File:By the Old Town Walls - Rhodes-1534091027.jpg
image.alt: Walking beside the Old Town's walls and dry moat

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding way to grasp the fortifications' scale, following the partially open wall circuit and the dry moat below.
thingsToDo.tip: Wall access is seasonal and limited to certain days and hours — check current times before planning around it.

thingsToDo.title: Climb to the Acropolis of Lindos

image.file: File:Medieval gate of the acropolis of Lindos.jpg
image.alt: The medieval gate leading up to the Acropolis of Lindos

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile climb above Lindos village, rewarded with ancient temple ruins, a medieval castle and sweeping bay views.
thingsToDo.tip: Start early morning or late afternoon — the climb offers genuinely little shade and midday summer heat is intense.

thingsToDo.title: Swim at Anthony Quinn Bay or Tsambika beach

image.file: File:Cape Ladhiko viewed from Anthony Quinn Bay Rhodes 16 September 2017.jpg
image.alt: The scenic cove of Anthony Quinn Bay

thingsToDo.text: Two of Rhodes' most striking beaches, the former a scenic cove named for the actor, the latter backed by dramatic cliffs.
thingsToDo.tip: Both beaches genuinely crowd by mid-morning in peak season — an early arrival secures a better spot.

thingsToDo.title: Take a day trip to Symi

image.alt: The pastel-coloured neoclassical houses of Symi

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely beautiful neighbouring island, its neoclassical harbour houses in pastel colours among the Dodecanese's most photogenic sights.
thingsToDo.tip: Boat trips typically include a stop at the Panormitis Monastery — a genuinely worthwhile addition to the day.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Rhodes Town beyond the Old Town

image.file: File:Saint Nicolas Fort Rhodes Harbour night.jpg
image.alt: The Fort of St Nicholas at the entrance to Mandraki harbour

thingsToDo.text: Rhodes Town's newer areas hold genuine interest too, from Mandraki harbour, where the Colossus of Rhodes is believed to have stood, to the town's historic Jewish Quarter.
thingsToDo.tip: Mandraki harbour's deer statues mark the Colossus's traditional, if archaeologically unconfirmed, location — worth knowing before you look for actual ruins.

thingsToDo.title: Go wine tasting around Embonas

image.alt: A vineyard in Rhodes' mountain wine country

thingsToDo.text: Rhodes' mountain wine country, centred on Embonas village, produces genuinely distinctive wines from the island's own Athiri and Mandilaria grapes.
thingsToDo.tip: Combine a winery visit with lunch in Embonas village, genuinely known for hearty, traditional mountain cooking.

foodIntro: Rhodian cuisine draws on the island's mountain villages and coastline alike, with several dishes genuinely distinct to the Dodecanese.

foods.name: Pitaroudia

image.alt: Pitaroudia, Rhodes' chickpea and courgette fritters

foods.text: Chickpea and courgette fritters seasoned with fresh herbs, a genuine Rhodes specialty found on nearly every taverna menu.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas across the island, a near-universal starter.

foods.name: Melekouni

image.alt: Melekouni, a dense sesame and honey sweet

foods.text: A dense sesame and honey sweet, traditionally served at Rhodian weddings, genuinely specific to the island's food culture.
foods.whereToTry: Old Town sweet shops and traditional bakeries across the island.

foods.name: Souma
foods.text: The Dodecanese's own grape-pomace spirit, similar to Crete's raki but genuinely distinct to Rhodes and its neighbouring islands.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas, often offered after a meal alongside dessert.

foods.name: Rhodian wine
foods.text: Wines from the island's own Athiri and Mandilaria grapes, particularly around the mountain village of Embonas, genuinely distinctive within Greek wine.
foods.whereToTry: Wineries around Embonas, and wine lists across the island's better tavernas.

foods.name: Stuffed courgette flowers

image.alt: Courgette flowers stuffed with rice and herbs

foods.text: Courgette blossoms filled with rice and herbs, a genuinely popular Rhodian taverna dish drawing on the island's productive market gardens.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas across the island, particularly in season through summer.

foods.name: Grilled octopus by the harbour

image.file: File:Octopus drying under the sun in Greece.jpg
image.alt: Octopus drying in the sun before grilling

foods.text: A genuine Rhodes Town staple, octopus dried in the sun before grilling, a classic sight and dish along Mandraki's waterfront tavernas.
foods.whereToTry: Harbourside tavernas in Rhodes Town, particularly around Mandraki.

accommodation.intro: Rhodes' right base depends on the balance you want between the Old Town's atmosphere, beach access and Lindos's quieter charm.

areas.name: Rhodes Town (Old Town or New Town)
areas.text: The island's most atmospheric and best-connected base, putting the Old Town, Mandraki harbour and transport links within easy reach.

areas.name: Lindos
areas.text: Genuinely charming but considerably smaller and quieter than Rhodes Town, with its own acropolis and beach on the doorstep.

areas.name: Faliraki or the east coast resorts
areas.text: Purpose-built resort areas offering genuinely direct beach access, at the cost of the Old Town's historic atmosphere.

gettingThere.intro: Rhodes has its own international airport, with ferries also connecting the island to Athens and the wider Dodecanese.

options.text: A short flight from [[athens|Athens]] reaches Rhodes in about an hour, the fastest option from the mainland.
options.detail: Book ahead in peak summer, when popular flight times can sell out or spike in price.

options.text: Overnight ferries from [[athens|Athens]]' port reach Rhodes in around 15–18 hours, a genuinely slow but scenic option via other islands.
options.detail: Cabin berths offer a genuinely comfortable way to arrive rested for the long overnight crossing.

options.mode: Ferry from Crete or other Dodecanese islands
options.text: Seasonal ferries connect Rhodes to [[crete|Crete]], alongside more frequent routes to Symi, Kos and other Dodecanese islands.
options.detail: Routes and frequency vary considerably by season — check current schedules before finalising an island-hopping itinerary.

gettingAround.intro: Rhodes Town and Lindos are both walkable individually, with buses and rental vehicles covering the wider island.

options.text: The most practical way to reach Lindos, Kamiros, Embonas and quieter beaches at your own pace.
options.detail: Mountain roads in the interior can be genuinely narrow and winding — allow more time than GPS estimates suggest.

options.text: A reliable network connects Rhodes Town to Lindos, Faliraki and other main towns along both coasts.
options.detail: Less frequent service to the mountainous interior — a car becomes genuinely useful for villages like Embonas.

options.text: A genuinely convenient option for Symi and other island day trips, which involve logistics easier left to a boat operator.
options.detail: Boat trips typically depart from Mandraki harbour each morning in season.

bestTime.headline: May–June and September, for warm weather without peak crowds
bestTime.summary: Rhodes enjoys one of Greece's longest sunny seasons, and shoulder season offers genuinely comparable weather with real relief from July and August's peak crowds.

seasons.text: Mild, increasingly warm weather with wildflowers across the countryside and noticeably thinner crowds than peak summer.
Hot and reliably sunny, genuinely the best swimming weather, but also the island's most crowded and expensive months.
Warm sea temperatures lingering from summer, comfortable air temperatures and noticeably thinner crowds.
Mild by northern European standards but genuinely too cool for swimming, with many resort-area businesses closed for the season.

bestTime.avoid: Peak July and August without accommodation booked well ahead, when Rhodes Town and Lindos both fill considerably and prices spike.

itinerary.title: Four days in Rhodes
itinerary.intro: The Old Town first, then Lindos, then the island's beaches and a taste of its wider Dodecanese connections.

days.title: Arrive in Rhodes Town
days.morning: Land and settle into Rhodes Town.
days.afternoon: The Old Town's walls, the Street of the Knights and the Palace of the Grand Master.

days.title: Lindos
days.summary: Ancient and medieval history above the sea.
days.morning: Travel to Lindos and climb to the Acropolis.
days.afternoon: Explore Lindos village and its beach.
days.evening: Return to Rhodes Town, or stay overnight in Lindos.

days.title: East coast beaches
days.morning: Swim at Tsambika or Anthony Quinn Bay.
days.afternoon: The Valley of the Butterflies, in season, or Ancient Kamiros.

days.title: Symi or wine country
days.summary: A final day beyond the main sights.
days.morning: A boat trip to Symi, or travel to Embonas.
days.afternoon: Symi's harbour town, or a wine tasting in Embonas.
days.evening: A final Rhodian dinner featuring pitaroudia and local wine.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on timing, transport and etiquette that make a real difference to a Rhodes trip.
tips: Book Old Town wall access in advance if possible — hours are seasonal and genuinely limited.
Visit Lindos's Acropolis early morning or late afternoon to avoid both the heat and the day-trip crowds.
Rent a car for at least part of the trip — Embonas, Kamiros and quieter beaches genuinely reward the flexibility.
Visit the Valley of the Butterflies between June and September for the moths — the main draw is genuinely seasonal.
Book accommodation ahead for peak summer, when both Rhodes Town and Lindos fill up considerably.
Wear proper shoes for Kamiros and the Acropolis of Lindos — both involve uneven ancient stonework.
Check ferry schedules for Symi and other Dodecanese day trips well ahead, especially outside peak summer.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Rhodes?
faq.a: Four to five for a first visit, enough to cover the Old Town, Lindos and the island's best beaches without feeling rushed.

faq.q: Is Rhodes worth visiting outside the Old Town?
faq.a: Genuinely, yes — Lindos, the east coast beaches and the mountain wine country around Embonas all reward time beyond Rhodes Town itself.

faq.q: Do I need a car in Rhodes?
faq.a: Helpful but not essential — buses cover Rhodes Town, Lindos and Faliraki reasonably well, though a car helps considerably for Kamiros, Embonas and quieter beaches.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit?
faq.a: May to June and September offer warm weather with crowds and prices well below the July-August peak, which is genuinely the island's busiest, hottest season.

faq.q: Can I visit other Dodecanese islands from Rhodes?
faq.a: Yes — Symi is a genuinely popular day trip, and ferries also connect Rhodes to Kos and other Dodecanese islands, with seasonal routes to Crete.
